title: A finite T0 space is sober
statement: Let $Y$ be a topological space whose underlying set is finite and which is $T_0$: for any two distinct points $y\ne y'$ of $Y$ there is an open subset of $Y$ containing exactly one of them. Then $Y$ is sober: for every irreducible closed subset $Z\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] there is exactly one point $\eta\in Z$ whose closure $\overline{\{\eta\}}$ in $Y$ equals $Z$.

source.place: Topology, the claim inside the proof of Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704) that the images X_J (finite subspaces of a finite product of two-point spaces) are finite sober spaces, which Stacks asserts without argument; sober = quasi-sober and Kolmogorov as in the paragraph after Definition label definition-generic-point (line 972, paragraph at line 989)

proof.text: *Step 1 (an irreducible set in a finite union of closed sets lies in one of them).* Let $Z\subseteq Y$ be irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] and let $F_1,\dots,F_n$ ($n\ge1$) be closed subsets of $Y$ with $Z\subseteq F_1\cup\dots\cup F_n$. We show by induction on $n$ that $Z\subseteq F_i$ for some $i$. For $n=1$ there is nothing to prove. For $n\ge2$ put $G=F_2\cup\dots\cup F_n$, closed in $Y$ as a finite union of closed sets. Then $Z=(Z\cap F_1)\cup(Z\cap G)$, and $Z\cap F_1$, $Z\cap G$ are closed in the subspace $Z$. As $Z$ is irreducible, $Z=Z\cap F_1$ or $Z=Z\cap G$, i.e. $Z\subseteq F_1$ or $Z\subseteq G=F_2\cup\dots\cup F_n$; in the second case the induction hypothesis (for $n-1$ sets) gives $Z\subseteq F_i$ for some $i\ge2$.

source.place: Topology, proof of Lemma Tag 09XX (label lemma-spectral-inverse-limit-finite-sober-spaces, line 4704): the images X_J are asserted to be finite sober spaces without argument; step written by the agent (the definition of irreducible, Definition Tag 004V, label definition-irreducible-components, line 855, applied n-1 times)

proof.text: *Step 2 (existence of a generic point).* Let $Z\subseteq Y$ be irreducible and closed. Then $Z$ is nonempty (irreducible sets are nonempty [def-weil-irreducible-components]) and finite ($Y$ is finite). For $z\in Z$ the closure $\overline{\{z\}}$ is closed, contains $z$, and is contained in $Z$ because $Z$ is a closed set containing $z$. Hence $Z=\bigcup_{z\in Z}\overline{\{z\}}$, a union of finitely many ($|Z|\ge1$) closed subsets of $Y$. By Step 1 there is $\eta\in Z$ with $Z\subseteq\overline{\{\eta\}}$; together with $\overline{\{\eta\}}\subseteq Z$ this gives $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$.
